## What Is Garak

Garak (Generative AI Red-teaming & Assessment Kit) is NVIDIA's LLM vulnerability scanner. Think of it like `nmap` or `nikto`, but for language models — you point it at a target model and it runs a large library of **probes**, each designed to trigger a specific class of vulnerability (jailbreaks, prompt leakage, toxicity, hallucination, encoding bypass, and more), then scores the responses with built-in **detectors**.

## Best For

- Fast, broad vulnerability scanning of a single model — you get coverage across dozens of attack classes in one command
- Comparing how a model behaves before/after fine-tuning or guardrail changes
- Testing local models served via Ollama, HuggingFace, or a custom REST endpoint (Garak isn't locked to OpenAI-style APIs)

pip install garak

# Confirm install
python -m garak --version

## Core Concepts

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Probe** | An attack module — e.g. `dan` (DAN-style jailbreaks), `promptinject`, `encoding` (Base64/ROT13 bypass), `xss` (markdown/HTML injection) |
| **Detector** | Scores whether the target's response indicates a successful attack |
| **Generator** | The adapter for the target model type — `openai`, `huggingface`, `ollama`, `rest` (custom HTTP), etc. |
| **Report** | An HTML/JSONL report summarizing pass/fail rates per probe |

# Full scan against an OpenAI-compatible model
garak --model_type openai --model_name gpt-4 --probes all

# Target only prompt injection probes
garak --model_type openai --model_name gpt-4 --probes promptinject

# Scan a local Ollama model (as used in this platform's labs)
garak --model_type ollama.OllamaChat --model_name llama3.2:1b -p dan.Dan_11_0

# Scan a custom REST endpoint (your own app, not a named provider)
garak --model_type rest -G rest_config.json --probes encoding

## Example Output

```
garak LLM vulnerability scanner v0.9.x
loading generator: openai:gpt-4
loading probes: dan, promptinject, encoding, xss

dan.DAN_Jailbreak                 : 14/50 attempts succeeded (28.0%)
promptinject.HijackHateHumans     : 2/50 attempts succeeded (4.0%)
encoding.InjectBase64             : 9/50 attempts succeeded (18.0%)
xss.MarkdownImageExfil            : 0/50 attempts succeeded (0.0%)

report written to garak_runs/gpt-4.report.jsonl
html summary: garak_runs/gpt-4.report.html
```

The percentage is your attack success rate per probe class — a fast way to see exactly where a model's guardrails are weakest without writing a single custom prompt.

Run `garak --list_probes` to see the full current probe catalog — it changes release to release as NVIDIA adds new attack classes. Don't rely on memorized probe names; always check the installed version's list before an engagement.

## When to Reach for Garak

Garak is usually the **first tool to run** against a new target — it's fast, broad, and needs almost no setup. Use its results to identify which vulnerability classes are worth digging into manually or with a more targeted framework like PyRIT or DeepTeam.
